data.title: Left for dead in the Amazon era, Toys "R" Us is growing again
Trump said to weigh range of options for lowering diesel costs without full export ban
data.description:
Trump administration officials are considering a range of measures to curb soaring diesel costs that would fall short of an outright ban on exports, and officials are working to announce a plan of action by early next week, according to multiple reports Friday.

One of the reported potential options would boost distribution of "dyed diesel," a red-colored fuel typically used by farmers and other off-road consumers and is tax-exempt; some state governors have already implemented this move.

The White House would also encourage more states to eliminate their state-level excise taxes on diesel ahead of the midterm elections, reports said.

Suspending any federal taxes on fuel would require action from Congress, which is highly unlikely since Republican leaders in the House have canceled remaining votes before the midterms, and a fight over whether to suspend the federal gas tax died in the House before the chamber left earlier this month.

White House conversations have included Vice President Vance, who reportedly favors a diesel export ban, and Energy Secretary Chris Wright, who has warned that an export ban would ultimately lead to higher fuel prices and has said he is seeking voluntary moves from refiners to provide some relief.

Key overseas allies, especially in Europe, are growing alarmed about the economic fallout from losing access to U.S. supplies at a time when wars in Iran and Ukraine have sapped global fuel availability.

European Union energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen has asked President Trump to maintain a "free flow" of diesel and warned that Europe's winter could be "very, very bad" for energy prices even without a ban on U.S. diesel.

Crude oil futures settled lower on Friday, with the market cautiously weighing diplomatic efforts seeking a U.S.-Iran agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under conditions that include the lifting of the U.S. Navy's blockade that has kept Iranian oil shut in.

"What are the chances of that? Slim to none, basically," Mizuho commodity specialist Robert Yawger said. "We've heard this story at least four times before, and it never panned out."

Furthermore, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are urging the Trump administration to maintain economic pressure on Iran and avoid concessions that would ease sanctions or the U.S. naval blockade, The Wall Street Journal reported.

On Friday, front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for November delivery fell 2.3% to $92.41/bbl, front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for November delivery lost 2.1% to $104.32/bbl; for the full week, Nymex crude declined 3.8% but Brent crude edged 0.4% higher.

U.S. natural gas futures (NG1:COM) gave back some of the previous session's gains prompted by the outage on a key pipeline in West Virginia, with the front-month October contract slipping 3.1% to $3.1960/MMBtu; for the week, natgas jumped 9.7%.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), fell 3.5% this week.

data.title: U.S. grain futures pull back from sharp losses with China ag deal news pending
data.description:
U.S. grain markets clawed back from early losses Friday after U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said details from President Trump's meeting with China's President Xi will be released on Monday.

CBOT grains had tumbled after the summit in Washington offered little information on hoped-for U.S.-China trade agreements in agriculture, including Chinese purchases of U.S. crops.

Trump said Thursday that the two leaders had made "tremendous strides" on expanding access to the Chinese market for U.S. farmers, but traders were disappointed by the lack of new information.

Chinese buyers have stepped up purchases of U.S. soybeans and are more than halfway toward the government's target to import 25M tons/year—a pledge that runs through 2028—but progress on a wider goal to buy at least $17B of U.S. agricultural products has been slower.

"Bull markets need to be fed daily, and no fresh news means a price correction to the downside has started," Total Farm Marketing's Naomi Blohm said in a note, but such a move should be "short-lived, due to overall smaller grain supplies globally," providing a potential buying opportunity for traders.

On Friday, CBOT wheat (W_1:COM) for December delivery closed 0.4% lower at $7.04 per bushel, while corn (C_1:COM) for December delivery ended 0.2% higher at $5.28 3/4 per bushel, and soybeans for November also added 0.2% to $13.20 per bushel.

Earlier in the session, CBOT soybeans had declined as much as 1%, extending losses to a fourth straight day, and corn and wheat both fell to one-month lows, dropping as much as 1.8% and 2.5%, respectively.

ETFs: (WEAT), (CORN), (SOYB), (DBA), (MOO)

data.title: Eli Lilly's Olumiant receives expanded alopecia indication for children 12 and up
data.description:
• The US FDA expanded the use of Eli Lilly's (LLY) Olumiant (baricitinib) for severe alopecia areata to include children 12 years and older.
  • Approval was based on 36-week data from the adolescent cohort of the phase 3 BRAVE-AA-PEDS study that showed those 80% or more scalp hair coverage was achieved in 42% of patients treated with Olumiant 4 mg and 27% treated with the 2 mg dosage, compared to 5% for those on placebo.
  • The JAK inhibitor is also approved for adults with rheumatoid arthritis.

data.title: Gold edges higher but falls for the week on hawkish Fed expectations
data.description:
Gold futures snapped a four-session losing streak Friday but ended with a weekly loss as a stronger dollar, surging Treasury yields, and growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again next month weighed on the metal.

U.S. Treasury yields posted multiyear highs this week, with the two-year, 10-year, and 20-year yields all rising sharply to end at 4.862%, 5.180%, and 5.500%, respectively.

"Investment metals faced a bond-market stress test, with surging Treasury yields supporting a stronger dollar and raising the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets," Saxo Bank analysts said in a note.

The ⁠Fed raised interest rates by a quarter-point last week, its first increase in three years, and traders are pricing in a 66% chance of an October hike and a 93% chance of an increase in December, according to CME's FedWatch ​Tool.

Front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for September delivery added 0.5% on Friday to $4,286.20/oz, and front-month Comex September silver (XAGUSD:CUR) climbed 1.2% to $64.245/oz; for the week, gold and silver fell 2.3% and 3.5%, respectively.

data.title: Northrop Grumman's strategic deterrent deal gets $111.4M boost
data.description:
• Northrop Grumman's (NOC) system unit announced on Friday that it received a ~$111.4M contract modification for the Ground-Based Strategic Deterrent engineering, manufacturing, and early production program.
  • The modification now brings the contract’s total value to $13.47B.
  • Moreover, the work will be performed in New Jersey and North Carolina and is expected to continue through Dec. 31, 2033.
  • The full $111.4M is being obligated through fiscal 2025 missile procurement funds.
  • The Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center is the contracting activity.

data.title: Southland Holdings receives NYSE American compliance notice
data.description:
• Southland Holdings (SLND) received a notice that it is no longer compliant with NYSE American’s stockholders’ equity requirements.
  • The company reported a $248.2M stockholders’ deficit as of June 30, 2026, alongside net losses in each of its last three fiscal years.
  • Southland must submit a compliance plan by October 23, 2026, outlining steps to regain compliance by March 23, 2028.
  • If the plan is not submitted or accepted, delisting proceedings may begin, while failure to regain compliance by March 23, 2028, could also trigger delisting proceedings.

data.title: Rio Tinto gets up to $995M defense logistics deal: Details inside
data.description:
• Rio Tinto Group (RIO)'s unit, Rio Tinto Logistics, won a maximum $995M IDIQ contract on Friday for high-purity aluminum.
  • The five-year contract has no option periods and runs through May 7, 2031.
  • The contract is funded with fiscal 2025–2029 transaction funds and was awarded by the Defense Logistics Agency Contracting Services Office.

data.title: Metallus wins up to $995M defense contract for high-fragmentation steel
data.description:
• Metallus (MUS) was awarded a maximum $995M U.S. defense contract for High Fragmentation 1 Steel.
  • The five-year contract runs through Sept. 24, 2031, with no option periods.
  • The funding comes from fiscal 2025–2029 transaction funds under the contract, with the DLA Contracting Services Office serving as the contracting activity.

data.title: Kongsberg Gruppen boosts U.S. defense push with $404M missile deal
data.description:
• Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace, a unit of Kongsberg Gruppen (NSKFF), won a $404.4M U.S. defense IDIQ contract for Naval Strike Missile launcher units, weapon control systems, and related support equipment.
  • The contract covers full-rate production and sustainment support through Sept. 24, 2034.
  • No funds were committed at award, while payments will be made through individual delivery and task orders as they are issued.
  • Portfolio Acquisition Executive, Marine Corps, is the contracting activity.
